motivation: the one published signal I found and never tested: structure-based rather than indicator-based, 3:1 payoff, 20-day holds, ~12 turns/year

signal_test.finding: the apparent significance was an artifact of overlapping forward-return windows. Consecutive observations share 19 of 20 days and are not independent samples. Corrected t-statistics are 0.09 and 0.07, i.e. no edge.
signal_test.methodological_bug: this flaw applies to my earlier rank-IC study too, which is why the momentum result also failed its holdout

constant_exposure_construction.description: always hold 20 names, W-curve detections chosen first, remainder filled by 250-day momentum, 20-day holds
constant_exposure_construction.verdict: full sample beat beta by 8.98 points with higher Sharpe; holdout lost to beta by 3.56 points. Classic full-period illusion.

exit_analysis.finding: only 4.1% of 20-bar windows in large caps contain both -5% and +15%, so a 15% target is structurally unreachable; the published result relied on a 2600-stock universe including small caps where such moves are common.

cross_cutting_lesson: eight strategy families have now been tested. The recurring failure is not weak signals, it is that full-sample statistics on Indian equities 2019-2026 are dominated by the 2020-2021 rally, and overlapping-window significance testing inflates apparent edge by roughly an order of magnitude.
